species.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redesign images 1 and 2, the existing ANGELFISH animation sprites. Images 3 and 4, the goldfish and betta, are STYLE REFERENCES showing the just-updated AQUABIT art direction. Match their thin navy outline, distinct animal anatomy, tiny carefully placed flat highlight clusters and readable retro pixel shapes; remain simple handmade low-resolution pixel art. Subject: a bright cyan freshwater angelfish with a vertically tall triangular silver-cyan body, elegant pointed dorsal and anal fins, two thin trailing ventral fin threads, dark blue fin ray details, a pale pearly belly, small black pixel eye with white highlight. In pose two change only the tail and fin tips, leaving the face and torso fixed. Fit tall fins inside 32 rows. Output ONE horizontal TWO-FRAME transparent RGBA sprite strip: logical 96x32 pixels (two adjacent 48x32 cells). An integer nearest-neighbor enlargement is okay; final game files will be 48x32 each. Both animals face LEFT, entire body stays within its cell with transparent margins. Keep each frame same size, head and torso position, logical pixel grid and colors. Body center around local x24 y18, room above head for a small accessory. NO accessories in the artwork. True transparent alpha background, no visible checkerboard, no text, labels or frames. No gradients, bloom, shadow, brush texture, glossy 3D, or antialiasing. Every mark should be a clear small square pixel. Preserve the fine one-pixel feeling of the original angelfish, but give the final sprites the richer anatomy and highlight detail of reference images 3 and 4.
